```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PLOT 2: SUMMARY STATISTICS - Taxa Counts
# ============================================================================

plot_gf_summary_stats <- function(gf_results) {
  
  # Calculate summary stats
  summary_data <- gf_results$combined %>%
    group_by(Kingdom, Soil) %>%
    summarise(
      n_taxa = n(),
      taxa_50pct = {
        cumsum_imp <- cumsum(sort(improve.tot, decreasing = TRUE)) / sum(improve.tot)
        sum(cumsum_imp <= 0.5)
      },
      taxa_80pct = {
        cumsum_imp <- cumsum(sort(improve.tot, decreasing = TRUE)) / sum(improve.tot)
        sum(cumsum_imp <= 0.8)
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = Kingdom, y = n_taxa, fill = Soil)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
             width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_taxa),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
              vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Cereal-dominated" = "#E41A1C", "Mixed-system" = "#377EB8"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(summary_data$n_taxa) * 1.15), 
                      expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Number of Important Taxa",
      subtitle = "Taxa with importance > 0"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, face = "italic")
    )
  
  return(p)
}

# ============================================================================

plot_gf_top_taxa <- function(gf_results, kingdom_filter, n_taxa = 10) {
  
  # Get top taxa per soil
  data <- gf_results$combined %>%
    filter(Kingdom == kingdom_filter) %>%
    group_by(Soil) %>%
    slice_max(order_by = improve.tot, n = n_taxa) %>%
    mutate(
      importance_pct = 100 * improve.tot / sum(improve.tot),
      spec_short = gsub("Cluster_", "C", spec)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      spec_short = factor(spec_short, levels = unique(spec_short))
    )
  
  # Plot
  p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = importance_pct, y = reorder(spec_short, importance_pct), 
                        fill = Soil)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Cereal-dominated" = "#E41A1C", "Mixed-system" = "#377EB8"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    labs(
      x = "Relative Importance (%)",
      y = NULL,
      title = sprintf("Top %d %s Taxa", n_taxa, kingdom_filter)
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~Soil, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90"),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 11)
    )
  
  return(p)
}

p_top_bacteria <- plot_gf_top_taxa(gf_results, "Bacteria", n_taxa = 10)
p_top_fungi <- plot_gf_top_taxa(gf_results, "Fungi", n_taxa = 8)

# Save top taxa plots
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "GF_top_taxa_bacteria.pdf"),

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "GF_top_taxa_fungi.pdf"),

# ============================================================================
# PLOT 4: SIMPLIFIED PANEL FOR MAIN FIGURE (RECOMMENDED)
# ============================================================================

# This shows just the key message in minimal space
plot_gf_minimal_panel <- function(gf_results) {
  
  # Calculate taxa needed for 50% and 80% cumulative importance
  summary_data <- gf_results$combined %>%
    group_by(Kingdom, Soil) %>%
    summarise(
      total_taxa = n(),
      taxa_50pct = {
        sorted_imp <- sort(improve.tot, decreasing = TRUE)
        cumsum_imp <- cumsum(sorted_imp) / sum(sorted_imp)
        sum(cumsum_imp <= 0.5) + 1  # +1 to include the taxa that crosses threshold
      },
      taxa_80pct = {
        sorted_imp <- sort(improve.tot, decreasing = TRUE)
        cumsum_imp <- cumsum(sorted_imp) / sum(sorted_imp)
        sum(cumsum_imp <= 0.8) + 1
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      pct_50 = 100 * taxa_50pct / total_taxa,
      pct_80 = 100 * taxa_80pct / total_taxa
    )
  
  # Reshape for plotting
  data_long <- summary_data %>%
    select(Kingdom, Soil, taxa_50pct, taxa_80pct) %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = c(taxa_50pct, taxa_80pct),
                 names_to = "threshold",
                 values_to = "n_taxa") %>%
    mutate(
      threshold_label = ifelse(threshold == "taxa_50pct", "50%", "80%")
    )
  
  # Create plot
  p <- ggplot(data_long, aes(x = Kingdom, y = n_taxa, fill = Soil)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
             width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n_taxa),
              position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
              vjust = -0.5, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Cereal-dominated" = "#E41A1C", "Mixed-system" = "#377EB8"),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(data_long$n_taxa) * 1.2), 
                      expand = c(0, 0)) +
    facet_wrap(~threshold_label, ncol = 2) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Number of Taxa",
      subtitle = "Taxa needed to explain cumulative importance"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, face = "italic"),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90")
    )
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to diagnose a GF object
diagnose_gf <- function(obj, name) {
  cat(sprintf("--- Checking: %s ---\n", name))
  
  # Check if it's a list
  cat(sprintf("  Type: %s\n", class(obj)[1]))
  
  if (is.list(obj)) {
    cat("  Structure: List with components:\n")
    cat(sprintf("    %s\n", paste(names(obj), collapse = ", ")))
    
    # Check for common components
    if ("gf_result" %in% names(obj)) {
      cat("  ✓ Found 'gf_result' component\n")
      cat(sprintf("    gf_result class: %s\n", class(obj$gf_result)[1]))
      
      # Check if gf_result is the actual GF object
      if ("gradientForest" %in% class(obj$gf_result)) {
        cat("  ✓ gf_result IS a gradientForest object!\n")
        cat("  → Solution: Use obj$gf_result for plotting\n")
        return(obj$gf_result)
      }
    }
    
    # Check if the list itself is a GF object
    if ("gradientForest" %in% class(obj)) {
      cat("  ✓ Object IS a gradientForest!\n")
      cat("  → Solution: Use obj directly for plotting\n")
      return(obj)
    }
    
    # Check each component
    for (comp_name in names(obj)) {
      comp <- obj[[comp_name]]
      if ("gradientForest" %in% class(comp)) {
        cat(sprintf("  ✓ Found gradientForest in '%s' component!\n", comp_name))
        cat(sprintf("  → Solution: Use obj$%s for plotting\n", comp_name))
        return(comp)
      }
    }
    
    cat("  ✗ No gradientForest object found in any component\n")
    return(NULL)
    
  } else if ("gradientForest" %in% class(obj)) {
    cat("  ✓ This IS a gradientForest object!\n")
    cat("  → Solution: Use obj directly for plotting\n")
    return(obj)
  } else {
    cat("  ✗ Not a list and not a gradientForest object\n")
    cat(sprintf("    Actual class: %s\n", paste(class(obj), collapse = ", ")))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  cat("\n")
}

cat("\n=== TESTING FIXED OBJECTS ===\n\n")

test_plot <- function(obj, name) {
  if (is.null(obj)) {
    cat(sprintf("✗ %s: No valid GF object found\n", name))
    return(FALSE)
  }
  
  tryCatch({
    # Try to plot with type O (overall importance)
    pdf(NULL)  # Suppress output
    plot(obj, plot.type = "O")
    dev.off()
    cat(sprintf("✓ %s: Plot works!\n", name))
    return(TRUE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("✗ %s: Plot failed - %s\n", name, e$message))
    return(FALSE)
  })
}

fungi_B_ok <- test_plot(gf_fungi_B_fixed, "Fungi mixed")
```

```{r}
cat("STEP 3: Creating turnover function plots...\n\n")

# Function to create one turnover plot
create_turnover_plot <- function(gf_obj, title, filename, n_species = 5) {
  
  cat(sprintf("  Creating: %s\n", filename))
  
  # Get importance and rank species
  imp <- importance(gf_obj)
  
  # Handle different return types
  if (is.matrix(imp) || is.data.frame(imp)) {
    if ("Weighted.Importance" %in% colnames(imp)) {
      by_importance <- rownames(imp)[order(imp[, "Weighted.Importance"], decreasing = TRUE)]
    } else {
      by_importance <- rownames(imp)[order(imp[, 1], decreasing = TRUE)]
    }
  } else if (is.vector(imp)) {
    by_importance <- names(sort(imp, decreasing = TRUE))
  }
  
  # Create plot
  pdf(file.path(fig_dir, filename), width = 6, height = 5)
  
  plot(gf_obj, 
       plot.type = "C",
       imp.vars = by_importance,
       show.overall = FALSE,
       legend = TRUE,
       leg.posn = "topleft",
       leg.nspecies = n_species,
       cex.lab = 0.9,
       cex.legend = 0.7,
       cex.axis = 0.8,
       line.ylab = 1.2,
       par.args = list(
         mgp = c(2, 0.7, 0),
         mar = c(3.5, 3.5, 2, 1)
       ),
       main = title
  )
  
  dev.off()
  
  cat(sprintf("    ✓ Saved: %s\n", filename))
}

# Create individual plots
create_turnover_plot(gf_bacteria_A_corrected, 
                     "Bacteria - Cereal-dominated", 
                     "GF_turnover_bacteria_cereal.pdf", 
                     n_species = 5)

create_turnover_plot(gf_bacteria_B_corrected, 
                     "Bacteria - Mixed-system", 
                     "GF_turnover_bacteria_mixed.pdf",
```

```{r - titan - whole dataset}
library(phyloseq)
library(TITAN2)

# Step 1: Define Output Directory
output_dir_full <- file.path(mypath_res, "TITAN_Full_Dataset")
if (!dir.exists(output_dir_full)) {
  dir.create(output_dir_full, recursive = TRUE)  # Create the directory if it doesn't exist
}

physeq_titan <- subset_samples(physeq, soil == "Permissive")  # Adjust to "resistant" "Permissive" or "resistant" if needed
# physeq_titan <- physeq_soilA

# OTU table as community matrix (samples x taxa)
community_matrix <- as.matrix(otu_table(physeq_titan))
if (taxa_are_rows(physeq_titan)) {
  community_matrix <- t(community_matrix)  # Ensure taxa are columns
}

# Step 3: Extract Environmental Gradient
# Replace "your_gradient_column" with the appropriate column name from your metadata
metadata <- sample_data(physeq_titan)
gradient <- metadata$Dry_wheat_mass  # Replace with the actual column name

# Ensure the gradient is numeric
gradient <- as.numeric(as.character(gradient))

# Step 4: Handle Missing Values
# Remove samples with missing values in the gradient
valid_samples <- !is.na(gradient)  # Logical vector for valid samples
community_matrix_clean <- community_matrix[valid_samples, ]
gradient_clean <- gradient[valid_samples]

# Step 5: Filter Rare Taxa
# Retain only taxa that occur in at least 3 samples
taxa_occurrence <- colSums(community_matrix_clean > 0)  # Count occurrences
community_matrix_filtered <- community_matrix_clean[, taxa_occurrence >= 10]

# Step 6: Run TITAN
titan_result_soilB <- titan(
  env = gradient_clean,
  txa = community_matrix_filtered,
  pur.cut = 0.95,       # Purity threshold (default 0.95)
  rel.cut = 0.95,       # Reliability threshold (default 0.95)
  minSplt = 5,          # Minimum split size
  nBoot = 500,          # Number of bootstrap replicates
  boot = TRUE,          # Perform bootstrap analysis
  imax = FALSE,         # Use sumz (default)
  ivTot = FALSE,        # Calculate indicator value by sumz
  ncpus = 1,            # Number of CPUs (increase if possible)
  messaging = TRUE      # Enable messages
)

# titan_result_full_purity0.8_reliabiliy.8 <- titan_result_full

# Step 7: Summarize Results
# View summary of TITAN results
summary(titan_result_soilB)
output_dir_full <- file.path(mypath_res, "TITAN_Full_Dataset")

# write.csv(titan_result_soilA$sppmax, file.path(output_dir_full, "bacteria_titan_soilA_results_v3.csv"), row.names = TRUE)




write.csv(titan_result_soilB$sppmax, file.path(output_dir_full, "bacteria_titan_soilB_results_v3.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
# Step 9: Extract Significant Indicator Taxa
# Extract sppmax from TITAN results
sppmax <- titan_result_full$sppmax
high_conf_taxa <- sppmax[sppmax$maxgrp == 2 & sppmax$purity > 0.9 & sppmax$reliability > 0.9, ]
high_conf_taxa <- sppmax[sppmax$purity > 0.95 & sppmax$reliability > 0.95, ]
high_conf_taxa_purity <- sppmax[sppmax$maxgrp == 2 & sppmax$purity > 0.95, ]

# Step 10: Save Significant Results
# Save positive and negative taxa to CSV
write.csv(high_conf_taxa, file.path(output_dir_full, "bacteria_positive_taxa_full.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(negative_taxa_full, file.path(output_dir_full, "bacteria_negative_taxa_full.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Save the full TITAN results to a CSV file
write.csv(titan_result_full$sppmax, file.path(output_dir_full, "bacteria_titan_results_full.csv"), row.names = FALSE)


# declining (i.e., maxgrp== 1) ; increasing declining (i.e., maxgrp== 2) 

plot_sumz_density(titan_result_soilA, ribbon = FALSE, points = TRUE)
plot_sumz_density(titan_result_soilB, ribbon = FALSE, points = TRUE)

plot_sumz(titan_result_full, filter = TRUE)
plot_taxa_ridges(titan_result_full, axis.text.y = 8)
plot_taxa_ridges(titan_result_full, xlabel = expression(paste("Wheat biomass"), n_ytaxa = 50))
plot_taxa_ridges(titan_result_full, xlabel = expression(paste("wheat biomass")), z1 = FALSE) # only positive

plot_taxa_ridges(titan_result_full, xlabel = expression(paste("wheat biomass")), z1 = FALSE, z2_fill_high = "#56B1F7") # only positive


plot_taxa(titan_result_full, xlabel = expression(paste("wheat biomass")), cex.taxa = 0.5, cex = 1.25, cex.axis = 1.1, legend = FALSE, col1 = "black", col2 = "red", fil2 = "red")
plot_cps(titan_result_full, taxaID = "Cluster_462", xlabel = "wheat biomass")
plot_cps(titan_result_full, taxaID = "Cluster_1155", cp.trace = TRUE, xlabel = "wheat biomass")
```

```{r}
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION - ADJUST THESE PATHS
# ============================================================================

titan_dir <- ""
output_dir <- file.path(titan_dir, "validation_plots")
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Load your phyloseq object to get metadata
# Adjust this to however you load your data
# physeq_bacteria <- readRDS("path/to/your/physeq_bacteria.rds")
# OR if already in environment, just use it directly

# ============================================================================
# LOAD TITAN2 RESULTS FROM CSV FILES
# ============================================================================

# Read all four TITAN2 result files
titan_files <- data.frame(
  kingdom = c("bacteria", "bacteria", "fungi", "fungi"),
  soil = c("resistant", "Permissive", "resistant", "Permissive"),
  soil_code = c("soilA", "soilB", "soilA", "soilB"),
  file = c(
    "bacteria_titan_soilA_results_v3.csv",
    "bacteria_titan_soilB_results_v3.csv",
    "fungi_titan_soilA_results_v3.csv",
    "fungi_titan_soilB_results_v3.csv"
  )
)

# Read and combine all TITAN2 results
titan_list <- lapply(1:nrow(titan_files), function(i) {
  filepath <- file.path(titan_dir, titan_files$file[i])
  
  if (!file.exists(filepath)) {
    warning(sprintf("File not found: %s", filepath))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  df <- read.csv(filepath, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
  
  # Add metadata columns
  df$taxa <- rownames(df)
  df$kingdom <- titan_files$kingdom[i]
  df$soil <- titan_files$soil[i]
  
  return(df)
})

# Combine all results
titan_all <- bind_rows(titan_list)

cat(sprintf("Loaded %d total taxa from TITAN2 results\n", nrow(titan_all)))
cat(sprintf("  Bacteria resistant: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_all$kingdom == "bacteria" & titan_all$soil == "resistant")))
cat(sprintf("  Bacteria Permissive: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_all$kingdom == "bacteria" & titan_all$soil == "Permissive")))
cat(sprintf("  Fungi resistant: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_all$kingdom == "fungi" & titan_all$soil == "resistant")))
cat(sprintf("  Fungi Permissive: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_all$kingdom == "fungi" & titan_all$soil == "Permissive")))

# ============================================================================
# FILTER TO HIGH-QUALITY INDICATORS
# ============================================================================

# Keep only taxa that pass TITAN2 filters (purity > 0.95, reliability > 0.95)
titan_keep <- titan_all %>%
  filter(
    filter == 1,  # TITAN2's built-in filter
    !is.na(ienv.cp),
    !is.na(zscore),
    purity > 0.95,
    reliability > 0.95
  )

cat(sprintf("\nAfter filtering (purity > 0.95, reliability > 0.95):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Total filtered taxa: %d\n", nrow(titan_keep)))
cat(sprintf("  Bacteria resistant: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_keep$kingdom == "bacteria" & titan_keep$soil == "resistant")))
cat(sprintf("  Bacteria Permissive: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_keep$kingdom == "bacteria" & titan_keep$soil == "Permissive")))
cat(sprintf("  Fungi resistant: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_keep$kingdom == "fungi" & titan_keep$soil == "resistant")))
cat(sprintf("  Fungi Permissive: %d taxa\n", 
            sum(titan_keep$kingdom == "fungi" & titan_keep$soil == "Permissive")))

# ============================================================================
# GET BIOMASS RANGE FROM YOUR DATA
# ============================================================================

# Extract metadata from phyloseq object
# Adjust this based on how you access your metadata
metadata_bact <- data.frame(sample_data(physeq_bacteria))
metadata_fungi <- data.frame(sample_data(physeq_fungi))

# Combine and get biomass range by soil
biomass_range <- bind_rows(
  metadata_bact %>% mutate(kingdom = "bacteria"),
  metadata_fungi %>% mutate(kingdom = "fungi")
) %>%
  group_by(soil) %>%
  summarise(
    n_samples = n(),
    biomass_min = min(Dry_wheat_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    biomass_max = max(Dry_wheat_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    biomass_mean = mean(Dry_wheat_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    biomass_median = median(Dry_wheat_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    biomass_sd = sd(Dry_wheat_mass, na.rm = TRUE),
    biomass_q25 = quantile(Dry_wheat_mass, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    biomass_q75 = quantile(Dry_wheat_mass, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\n=== BIOMASS RANGE BY SOIL ===\n")
print(biomass_range)
```



```{r}
# ============================================================================
# VALIDATE CHANGE-POINTS ARE WITHIN BIOMASS RANGE
# ============================================================================

# Summarize change-point distribution
cp_summary <- titan_keep %>%
  group_by(kingdom, soil) %>%
  summarise(
    n_taxa = n(),
    cp_min = min(ienv.cp),
    cp_q25 = quantile(ienv.cp, 0.25),
    cp_median = median(ienv.cp),
    cp_q75 = quantile(ienv.cp, 0.75),
    cp_max = max(ienv.cp),
    cp_mean = mean(ienv.cp),
    cp_sd = sd(ienv.cp),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Merge with biomass range
cp_validation <- cp_summary %>%
  left_join(biomass_range, by = "soil")

cat("\n=== CHANGE-POINT DISTRIBUTION ===\n")
print(cp_validation %>%
        select(kingdom, soil, n_taxa, cp_median, cp_min, cp_max, 
               biomass_median, biomass_min, biomass_max))

# Check for change-points outside biomass range
extreme_cps <- titan_keep %>%
  left_join(biomass_range, by = "soil") %>%
  mutate(
    outside_range = ienv.cp < biomass_min | ienv.cp > biomass_max,
    at_extreme = ienv.cp < biomass_q25 | ienv.cp > biomass_q75
  )

n_outside <- sum(extreme_cps$outside_range)
n_extreme <- sum(extreme_cps$at_extreme)
pct_outside <- round(100 * n_outside / nrow(titan_keep), 1)
pct_extreme <- round(100 * n_extreme / nrow(titan_keep), 1)

cat(sprintf("\n=== VALIDATION SUMMARY ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Taxa with CP outside biomass range: %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_outside, pct_outside))
cat(sprintf("Taxa with CP at extremes (<Q25 or >Q75): %d (%.1f%%)\n", n_extreme, pct_extreme))

if (n_outside > 0) {
  cat("\nWARNING: Some change-points fall outside observed biomass range:\n")
  print(extreme_cps %>%
          filter(outside_range) %>%
          select(kingdom, soil, taxa, ienv.cp, zscore, biomass_min, biomass_max) %>%
          head(20))
} else {
  cat("\n✓ All change-points fall within observed biomass range\n")
}
```

How to Characterize the High-Biomass Responses

mypath <- "/Users/mathieuvanhove/Desktop/Work/DeepImpact/Weeds_wheat/paper_1/data/results_v4/"


```{r}
# Reload TITAN2 data
titan_keep <- titan_all %>%
  filter(filter == 1, purity > 0.95, reliability > 0.95,
         !is.na(ienv.cp), !is.na(zscore))

# Split into low-biomass vs high-biomass indicators
titan_classified <- titan_keep %>%
  mutate(
    cp_category = case_when(
      ienv.cp < 0.15 ~ "Low biomass (<0.15g) - Stress transition",
      ienv.cp >= 0.15 & ienv.cp < 0.35 ~ "Mid biomass (0.15-0.35g) - Moderate range",
      ienv.cp >= 0.35 ~ "High biomass (≥0.35g) - Growth-promoting range"
    )
  )

# Count indicators in each range
cp_summary <- titan_classified %>%
  group_by(kingdom, soil, cp_category) %>%
  summarise(
    n_taxa = n(),
    mean_zscore = mean(zscore),
    taxa_list = paste(head(taxa, 5), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("=== CHANGE-POINT DISTRIBUTION BY BIOMASS RANGE ===\n")
print(cp_summary)

# Identify high-biomass indicators
high_biomass_indicators <- titan_classified %>%
  filter(ienv.cp >= 0.35) %>%
  arrange(desc(zscore))


high_biomass_indicators

write.csv(high_biomass_indicators, file = paste(mypath, "TITAN_Full_Dataset/high_biomass_indicators.csv", sep=""), row.names = TRUE)  # Set row.names to FALSE if you don't want to save row names


cat("\n=== TOP HIGH-BIOMASS INDICATORS ===\n")
print(high_biomass_indicators %>%
        select(kingdom, soil, taxa, ienv.cp, zscore, freq, reliability) %>%
        head(20))

# Visualize the three ranges
ggplot(titan_classified, aes(x = ienv.cp, fill = cp_category)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  facet_grid(soil ~ kingdom) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Low biomass (<0.15g) - Stress transition" = "#d62728",
               "Mid biomass (0.15-0.35g) - Moderate range" = "#ff7f0e",
               "High biomass (≥0.35g) - Growth-promoting range" = "#2ca02c")
  ) +
  labs(title = "TITAN2 Change-Points Across Biomass Range",
       x = "Change-Point (g)", y = "Number of Taxa",
       fill = "Biomass Category") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "Fig_TITAN2_biomass_categories.pdf"),
       width = 12, height = 8)
```

1. Panel A: TITAN2 Figure

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)

# ============================================================================
# PANEL A: TITAN2 THRESHOLD INDICATORS (BOTH KINGDOMS)
# ============================================================================

# Assuming you already have:
# - titan_all: combined TITAN2 results from all soils/kingdoms
# - cp_medians: median change-points per soil/kingdom

# Classify by biomass category
titan_plot <- titan_all %>%
  filter(filter == 1, purity > 0.95, reliability > 0.95) %>%
  mutate(
    biomass_category = case_when(
      ienv.cp < 0.15 ~ "Low biomass (<0.15g)",
      ienv.cp >= 0.15 & ienv.cp < 0.35 ~ "Mid biomass (0.15-0.35g)",
      ienv.cp >= 0.35 ~ "High biomass (≥0.35g)"
    ),
    biomass_category = factor(
      biomass_category,
      levels = c("Low biomass (<0.15g)", 
                 "Mid biomass (0.15-0.35g)", 
                 "High biomass (≥0.35g)")
    ),
    soil_label = ifelse(soil == "resistant", "Cereal-dominated", "Mixed-system"),
    kingdom_label = tools::toTitleCase(kingdom)
  )

# Strategic labeling - label ALL green/orange fungi since they're rare
# For bacteria, label top 5 per category
titan_labels <- titan_plot %>%
  group_by(soil, kingdom, biomass_category) %>%
  mutate(
    should_label = case_when(
      # For fungi: label ALL mid and high biomass points (very few)
      kingdom == "fungi" & biomass_category %in% c("High biomass (≥0.35g)", 
                                                     "Mid biomass (0.15-0.35g)") ~ TRUE,
      # For bacteria: label top 5 by z-score per category
      kingdom == "bacteria" ~ rank(-abs(zscore)) <= 5,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(should_label) %>%
  ungroup()

# Create plot
panel_A <- ggplot(titan_plot, aes(x = ienv.cp, y = zscore)) +
  # Median CP line
  geom_vline(
    data = cp_medians %>%
      mutate(soil_label = ifelse(soil == "resistant", 
                                  "Cereal-dominated", "Mixed-system"),
             kingdom_label = tools::toTitleCase(kingdom)),
    aes(xintercept = cp_median),
    linetype = "dotted", color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  # Points colored by biomass category
  geom_point(aes(size = freq, alpha = reliability, color = biomass_category)) +
  # Labels
  geom_text_repel(
    data = titan_labels,
    aes(label = taxa, color = biomass_category),
    size = 2.2,
    max.overlaps = 25,
    box.padding = 0.3,
    segment.alpha = 0.4,
    segment.size = 0.3,
    force = 1.5,
    min.segment.length = 0
  ) +
  # Facet: kingdom (rows) × soil (columns)
  facet_grid(kingdom_label ~ soil_label, scales = "free") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.5, 4), name = "Frequency") +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.3, 1), name = "Reliability") +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Biomass Category",
    values = c(
      "Low biomass (<0.15g)" = "#d62728",
      "Mid biomass (0.15-0.35g)" = "#ff7f0e",
      "High biomass (≥0.35g)" = "#2ca02c"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Change-Point along Wheat Biomass Gradient (g)",
    y = "Response Strength (z-score)"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )

# Save
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Panel_A_TITAN2.pdf"), 
  panel_A, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 8, 
  dpi = 300
)

print("Panel A saved successfully!")
```


2. Panel B: mEQO Data Import and Visualization (R Code)
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)

# ============================================================================
# LOAD mEQO DATA FOR BACTERIA AND FUNGI
# ============================================================================

eqo_folder <- file.path(mypath_res, "mEQO")

# Function to load and prepare mEQO data
load_meqo_data <- function(soil_letter, kingdom) {
  # Read files
  module_abundance <- read.csv(
    file.path(eqo_folder, sprintf("eqo_module_soil%s_abundance_%s.csv", 
                                  soil_letter, kingdom)),
    row.names = 1
  )
  
  dry_mass <- read.csv(
    file.path(eqo_folder, sprintf("dry_mass_soil%s_%s.csv", 
                                  soil_letter, kingdom))
  )
  
  # Combine
  df <- data.frame(
    Module_Abundance = module_abundance[, 1],
    Wheat_Biomass = dry_mass[, ncol(dry_mass)]  # Last column is biomass
  )
  
  # Add metadata
  df$Soil <- ifelse(soil_letter == "A", "Cereal-dominated", "Mixed-system")
  df$Kingdom <- tools::toTitleCase(kingdom)
  
  return(df)
}

# Load all combinations
bacteria_soilA <- load_meqo_data("A", "bacteria")
bacteria_soilB <- load_meqo_data("B", "bacteria")
fungi_soilA <- load_meqo_data("A", "fungi")
fungi_soilB <- load_meqo_data("B", "fungi")

# Combine
bacteria_data <- rbind(bacteria_soilA, bacteria_soilB)
fungi_data <- rbind(fungi_soilA, fungi_soilB)

# ============================================================================
# CALCULATE CORRELATIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bacteria
bacteria_stats <- bacteria_data %>%
  group_by(Soil) %>%
  summarise(
    rho = cor(Wheat_Biomass, Module_Abundance, method = "spearman"),
    p_value = cor.test(Wheat_Biomass, Module_Abundance, 
                       method = "spearman")$p.value,
    r2 = summary(lm(Module_Abundance ~ Wheat_Biomass))$r.squared,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Fungi
fungi_stats <- fungi_data %>%
  group_by(Soil) %>%
  summarise(
    rho = cor(Wheat_Biomass, Module_Abundance, method = "spearman"),
    p_value = cor.test(Wheat_Biomass, Module_Abundance, 
                       method = "spearman")$p.value,
    r2 = summary(lm(Module_Abundance ~ Wheat_Biomass))$r.squared,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print("Bacteria correlations:")
print(bacteria_stats)

print("Fungi correlations:")
print(fungi_stats)

# ============================================================================
# CREATE mEQO PLOTS
# ============================================================================

# Color scheme
soil_colors <- c("Cereal-dominated" = "#E41A1C", "Mixed-system" = "#377EB8")

# Create annotation text
bacteria_annotation <- sprintf(
  "R² = %.2f-%.2f\nρ = %.2f-%.2f",
  min(bacteria_stats$r2), max(bacteria_stats$r2),
  min(bacteria_stats$rho), max(bacteria_stats$rho)
)

fungi_annotation <- sprintf(
  "R² = %.2f-%.2f\nρ = %.2f-%.2f",
  min(fungi_stats$r2), max(fungi_stats$r2),
  min(fungi_stats$rho), max(fungi_stats$rho)
)

# Bacteria plot
plot_bacteria <- ggplot(bacteria_data, 
                        aes(x = Wheat_Biomass, y = Module_Abundance, color = Soil)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = soil_colors) +
  annotate("text", 
           x = Inf, y = Inf,
           label = bacteria_annotation,
           size = 3, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5,
           fontface = "italic") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "mEQO Module Abundance",
    subtitle = "Bacteria"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )

# Fungi plot
plot_fungi <- ggplot(fungi_data, 
                     aes(x = Wheat_Biomass, y = Module_Abundance, color = Soil)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, alpha = 0.2, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = soil_colors, name = "Soil Type") +
  annotate("text", 
           x = Inf, y = Inf,
           label = fungi_annotation,
           size = 3, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5,
           fontface = "italic") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "mEQO Module Abundance",
    subtitle = "Fungi"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )

# Combine
panel_B <- plot_bacteria + plot_fungi +
  plot_layout(ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(
    caption = "Wheat Biomass (g)",
    theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, 
                                              face = "bold", vjust = -1))
  )

# Save
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Panel_B_mEQO.pdf"), 
  panel_B, 
  width = 10, 
  height = 5, 
  dpi = 300
)

print("Panel B saved successfully!")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# PANEL C: SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

# Create summary data
summary_data <- data.frame(
  Kingdom = rep(c("Bacteria", "Fungi"), each = 2),
  Soil = rep(c("Cereal-dominated", "Mixed-system"), 2),
  Total_Indicators = c(437, 437, 116, 116),
  High_Biomass = c(15, 25, 1, 1)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Pct_High_Biomass = 100 * High_Biomass / Total_Indicators
  )

panel_C <- ggplot(summary_data, 
                  aes(x = Kingdom, y = Pct_High_Biomass, fill = Soil)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
           width = 0.7, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%\n(n=%d)", Pct_High_Biomass, High_Biomass)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Cereal-dominated" = "#E41A1C", "Mixed-system" = "#377EB8"),
    name = "Soil Type"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 25), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "High-Biomass Indicators\n(% of total)",
    title = "Proportion of Growth-Promoting Indicators"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold")
  )

# Save
ggsave(
  file.path(output_dir, "Panel_C_summary.pdf"), 
  panel_C, 
  width = 6, 
  height = 5, 
  dpi = 300
)
```
